title: N'th Element of a List

arguments.name: index
arguments.constraint: The source specifies nonnegative, zero-based lookup. For i >= 0, i is in bounds exactly when i < List.length xs. The public statement does not specify behavior for negative OCaml ints.

arguments.name: xs
arguments.constraint: Finite immutable OCaml list; preserves list order and duplicate occurrences.

guarantees: For index >= 0, returns Some x exactly when index < list length and x is the element at that zero-based list position.
For index >= 0, returns None exactly when index >= list length.
Negative-index behavior is source-unspecified and is intentionally not asserted by this benchmark contract or its tests.
Does not raise an out-of-bounds exception.

nonfunctional_constraints: For the stated nonnegative domain, no exceptions for index failure; failure is represented with None.
No requirement on strings or floats specifically; the element type is polymorphic.
